source_extracts.label: USPS Postal Explorer — Preparing Packages, Sealing
source_extracts.quote: Tape the opening of your box and reinforce all seams with 2-inch-wide tape. Use clear or brown packaging tape, reinforced packing tape, or paper tape. Do not use cord, string, twine, masking, or cellophane tape.

source_extracts.label: USPS national release — holiday shipping guidance
source_extracts.quote: Use pressure-sensitive tape, nylon-reinforced craft paper tape or glass-reinforced pressure-sensitive tape for shipping. Do not use wrapping paper, string, masking tape, duct tape or cellophane tape.

source_extracts.label: UPS — How To Ship a Package
source_extracts.quote: Then, seal your box with plastic or nylon tape at least two inches wide.

source_extracts.label: UPS — Packaging Tips, Only Use Shipping Tape
source_extracts.quote: Do not use masking, cellophane, duct or water activated paper tapes, string or paper over-wrap. Securely seal closures and seams.

source_extracts.label: FedEx — How to Pack, Sealing Your Package
source_extracts.quote: Use pressure-sensitive plastic tape, water-activated paper tape (minimum 60-lb. grade), or water-activated reinforced tape that is at least 2" wide. ... Use the H taping method. ... Do not use cellophane tape, duct tape, masking tape, string, or rope to seal packages.

numeric_claims.scope: Minimum tape width in inches required by USPS (DMM100 sealing: 2-inch-wide tape), UPS (plastic or nylon tape at least two inches wide), and FedEx (tape at least 2" wide) per the sources above. Corrects the original article's 3-inch FedEx claim.

The 3-inch FedEx width figure appears ONLY inside the explicit correction sentence ('an earlier version said FedEx wanted 3-inch tape; the guide says at least 2 inches') — it documents the old error, it is not a current requirement.
FedEx minimum grade for water-activated paper tape: 60-lb grade, per the FedEx How to Pack PDF.
Published Mailbox Plus counter price for a professional re-seal (owner-published since 2026-09-11).
Store street number, 7554 Fredle Drive, Concord Township, OH 44077 (siteConfig).
Spelled-out counts describing the H-taping pattern (one center strip plus a strip across each of the two end seams, top and bottom = three strips per side, per UPS/FedEx sealing guidance).

scope_rules: Each carrier rule is attributed to that carrier's own published guidance; USPS duct-tape prohibition is cited to the USPS national release, not the DMM100 page, which names only masking and cellophane.
The FedEx 3-inch figure from the 2026-09-11 original is corrected to 2 inches; no 3-inch width claim appears in the rewrite.
No claim about claim-denial outcomes or repack-bag procedures is asserted as carrier policy; consequences are framed as what the carriers' own written rules imply.
required_when: Any edit adding a tape width, tape grade, price, address, or phone number to this article must register it here first.
